title: Tiers started doing real work
summary:
User tiers began shaping image routing and queue behavior, while the APIs gained more control and the community showcase kept growing.

Seed, flower, and nectar tiers were added to the dashboard, with a flower-tier request option in the Special Bee form. Authenticated GPT Image requests now route by tier instead of randomly, and nectar requests skip the queue whether they arrive by token or registered referrer. Other token-authenticated requests get a zero queue interval. Unassigned users default to seed; the tier work did not add automatic upgrades or tier-based limits.

Text requests gained temperature, top_p, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty controls for OpenAI-compatible providers, with supplied values taking precedence over model defaults. Authenticated GET and POST /preferences endpoints were added for reading and updating settings. Text cache keys now ignore authentication and cache-control fields, so those fields alone no longer split otherwise identical requests.

The image API now accepts comma-separated reference URLs, and Azure GPT Image edit mode uses every supplied image rather than just the first. Edit uploads also use their Content-Type when naming files. A prompt-enhancement change reduced rate-limit interruptions that could interfere with translation of Chinese and other non-English prompts.

Text and image services now share authentication and queue handling, and invalid tokens return a 401 instead of crashing the text server. The auth dashboard gained a collapsible guide with web and backend examples, while accepted token formats were narrowed to the documented fields. Error logging also stopped failing on null message entries and hiding the original response.
